# PID visit detection: tuning guide and recall experiment

**Who this is for:** whoever decides the detection settings before the field trial (super admin, project owner).
**Generated by:** `DB_SCHEMA=perf_<x> npm run recall` (`be/scripts/recall-experiment.js`). It runs the **real detection engine** on simulated tracks in a throwaway schema.

> GPS proximity shows that a vehicle passed near a property. It never proves that garbage was collected (flow.txt §1, §8.5).

---

## 1. Summary

1. **With point-based detection and normal 30–60 s GPS intervals, a truck that drives past without stopping is almost never CONFIRMED.** At 30 s and 15 km/h, consecutive points are about 125 m apart, while a 30 m circle around a house only covers about 57 m of the road. Result: **0 % confirmed, ~33 % candidate, ~67 % missed** (2 out of 3 houses get no GPS point within 30 m at all).
2. **Precision is excellent:** "false-confirmed" is ≈ 0 % in every cell. When the engine says CONFIRMED, the vehicle really was within the radius.
3. **Real collection behaviour helps a lot.** With the truck stopping 30 s every 60 m, the same 30 s / 10 m setting gives **31.8 % confirmed, 57.1 % candidate, 11.2 % missed**. Garbage trucks do stop, so the field trial will probably look more like this row than like the drive-by rows.
4. **The biggest lever is the detection method, not the settings.** Checking the **line between consecutive GPS points** (segment-based) instead of only the points themselves would catch **~93 %** of truly passed houses at 30 s / 10 m. The trade-off is about 11 % false hits on houses further back. That is a code change; see §5.
5. The confirmation mode barely matters for drive-bys. `consecutive_points` and `min_events` give identical results here, and `dwell 20 s` confirms only stops.

## 2. What was simulated

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Streets | 20 straight streets, 1.2 km each, far apart |
| PIDs | 100 per street, one every 12 m, alternating sides, setbacks **10 / 18 / 26 / 34 / 42 m** from the street centre |
| Vehicle | Drives the street centreline at **15 km/h**, one pass. In the "stops" variant it also stops 30 s every 60 m |
| GPS | One point every Δt (10 / 30 / 60 s), random start phase, **uniform jitter** within the jitter radius |
| Ground truth | A PID is **truly passed** when its setback ≤ radius. At radius 30 that's the 10/18/26 m houses (60 %); 34/42 m are **neighbouring properties that must not be confirmed** |
| Engine | The real SQL engine (`pidDetectionService`), with stale-point gating off. The modes are run one after another on the same track |

Column meanings (percentages):
- **confirmed / candidate / missed:** of the truly passed PIDs, the share that ended CONFIRMED, CANDIDATE, or with no qualifying point (NOT_VISITED).
- **false-confirmed:** of the PIDs **not** truly passed, the share wrongly CONFIRMED.
- **false-any:** of the PIDs not truly passed, the share that got any status (CANDIDATE or CONFIRMED).
- **segment-based detect / false:** what a line-segment check *would* give on the same track (JS estimate, not implemented).

The radius-50 rows show "n/a" for the false columns because every simulated house (max 42 m) is truly passed at radius 50. A wider radius **will** reach neighbours in reality, so §4 caps it.

## 4. Recommendation for the field trial

**Settings to start with** (all editable at runtime: `PUT /api/settings/<key>`, SUPER_ADMIN):

| Setting | Start value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `detection.radius_m` | **30** | Keeps false hits on neighbouring houses near 0. Try 40 only if field trials show many CANDIDATE/missed on clearly visited streets. Avoid ≥ 50 on dense streets. |
| `detection.confirmation_mode` | **`consecutive_points`** (N = 2) | Same as `min_events` for drive-bys, and the clearest rule for officials. |
| `detection.consecutive_points` | **2** | 1 would turn every CANDIDATE into CONFIRMED, making confirmation meaningless. |
| `detection.max_gps_age_s` + `late_points_policy` | 300 s + **`evidence_only`** | Switch to `accept` only for trackers that **buffer offline and upload later** (check this with the provider), otherwise their whole route becomes REJECTED_STALE. |
| `detection.max_speed_kmh` | 40 | Ignores points from fast transit stretches (not a collection drive). |
| GPS poll interval | **as low as the provider allows; aim for ≤ 10–15 s** | The single most effective setting. 60 s misses ~83 % even when the truck passes. |

**How to report this to officials:**
- Show **"GPS visit detected" (CANDIDATE + CONFIRMED)** and **"GPS visit confirmed"** as two separate figures.
- Coverage % (flow §12) stays confirmed-only. At 30 s polling it will look very low unless the trucks stop at the properties; that reflects GPS limits, not truck performance.
- Never call either figure "collected".

**Field-trial protocol (1–2 weeks, 3–5 vehicles):**
1. Pick 2–3 routes and get **ground truth**: a supervisor rides along, or residents confirm, for 50–100 PIDs.
2. Record the provider's **real point interval** (`gps_poll_runs`, `gps_locations` timestamps) and estimate the jitter from points of a parked vehicle.
3. Compare the engine's statuses with the ground truth, using `GET /api/pid-visits/missed` and the daily summary.
4. Tune `radius_m` (30 → 40) and the interval. After each change, run `POST /api/detection/reprocess` for the trial days, so the same raw GPS is re-evaluated with the new settings.
5. Look at `ambiguous` events (one point within radius of 2+ PIDs). They mark dense streets, where houses can't be told apart by GPS at all.

## 5. Proposed improvement: segment-based proximity (needs approval)

Point-based detection only looks at where the GPS points are. It ignores where the vehicle obviously went **between** two points 125 m apart.

A segment check (the distance from the PID to the line between two consecutive points of the same vehicle, ≤ radius and with a sane gap/speed) gives **92.7 % detected at 30 s / 10 m, versus 33.1 %**. The cost is ~11 % false hits on houses 34–42 m back, rising with jitter (20.6 % at 20 m).

Proposal:
- Add segment proximity as a **separate, weaker evidence type** (e.g. `TRACK_SEGMENT`). It would make a PID at most **CANDIDATE**, never CONFIRMED by itself.
- Gate it on a maximum segment length and time gap (e.g. ≤ 200 m and ≤ 90 s), so GPS gaps and teleports don't create evidence.
- Keep CONFIRMED for point evidence (stops / slow passes). This keeps precision honest while cutting "missed" from ~67 % to ~7 %.

It fits the current set-based design: one extra CTE using `LAG` per vehicle and a segment-to-point distance in SQL.
